items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: I didn't make any records with Johnny Detroit. No? No, my brother, I don't think my brother made any of them.

ctx.x: And, uh, they didn't, didn't say, well, geez, are you a jazz man or what? Uh, point out what you, what you do? I mean, it's up to the guys, uh, to find out, uh, after, after you play, whatever you do, you know? Yeah. You know, whatever, you thought you could play some jazz? So, so that, that's when, uh, when Tony Perani had his band, they were playing at the, at the, at the Greenwald Grill downstairs, see? Mm-hmm. I don't know what it was, Johnny Bison, uh, Johnny Detroit's band down there first, and, uh, Santo…
Did the, did you have to have a test to get in the Union, in those days?

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: Raymond was playing at some cheap joint on Bourbon Street but he'd take his intermission at that time so he could rush in and open them with us at Cobb's.

ctx.x: Raymond used to sub, if my brother had a late show, I was making so much money I quit the office. It wasn't interesting anymore. You know I'm a leader. Because I had an outfit in Morrison's cafeteria. He used to have music there. I have outfits all over. And so if the off you had a late show, Raymond was playing at some cheap joint on Bourbon Street but he'd take his intermission at that time so he could rush in and open them with us at Cobb's. And my brother would give him a couple of dollars. And he was…
